solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Try first two parts of Aeneid, with Virgil in translation

indicators.note: a translation recasts the text, so these letters are rendered in a new order

parts.note: the first two letters of the word Aeneid
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A classics student is told to have a go at translating the opening of Virgil's epic.
explanation.walkthrough: AE (the start of Aeneid) plus WITH and VIRGIL is the twelve-letter pool that 'in translation' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a whirl is an informal idiom for attempting it, so it can stand for the verb try.

clue.text: Suffering greatly from onset of apoplectic fit in hotel yard

indicators.note: says the letters of apoplectic's start and fit go inside the hotel word

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel

indicators.note: the onset is the start, so only the opening letter of apoplectic is used

parts.note: first letter A
a go is a bout or turn, like a fit of something

explanation.surface: Someone collapses with a seizure in the yard of a hotel and is in great pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like a seizure, continuing the apoplexy, but a go is a bout or turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in agony is an idiom for experiencing extreme pain, which is what suffering greatly describes.

clue.text: Prominent Russian, having turned up in work unit, is becoming agitated

indicators.note: puts the jumbled name inside the unit of work

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics

indicators.note: turned up in the sense of upset, so a letter of the president's name is knocked out of place

parts.note: Vladimir Putin, the Russian president

explanation.surface: A powerful Russian arrives unannounced at a workplace and everyone gets flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads as arrived, but it means upset, rearranging the name; 'is' links to the definition, and 'in' places the result inside the unit of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Erupting describes bursting out with anger or emotion, a fair picture of someone growing agitated.

clue.text: Virginia could be appearing topless for art patron

indicators.note: without its top, so the opening letter is removed

parts.note: Virginia is an example of a US state

explanation.surface: A woman named Virginia might pose nude in front of a wealthy collector.
explanation.walkthrough: Virginia is not a woman here but a US state; STATE loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Tate, the sugar magnate, was a benefactor whose collection founded the Tate gallery in London.

clue.text: Actively seek the means to enlightenment? Or just have a look

definitions.text: Actively seek the means to enlightenment?
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: to go shopping for windows, which let in light
second meaning: to browse in shops without buying anything

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a joke: windows are what bring light into a room, so shopping for them seeks enlightenment; 'Or' joins the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: Window-shopping is the pastime of browsing displays in shop fronts without intending to purchase.

clue.text: Suffer curtailment of fashionable remedy

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: curtailing cuts off the tail, so the last letter of the phrase goes

parts.note: a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: A trendy treatment gets cut back and patients bear the consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to bring it on oneself and undergo it, a sense close to suffer.

clue.text: Bond's in Spain, tailing Russian barman, keeping his head down

indicators.note: following behind, so the Spain letter comes after the composer's name
in a down clue the first letter is sent to the bottom, the end of the name

parts.note: Mikhail Glinka, the Russian composer; a composer writes music in bars, so he is a bar man
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: James Bond is in Spain, shadowing a Russian bartender who is lying low.
explanation.walkthrough: The barman is no bartender but the Russian composer, a man of musical bars; in a down entry his head goes to the bottom. 'Bond's in' reads as 007, but Bond is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond is a connection or tie, and a linkage is likewise something that joins two things together.

clue.text: Capricious hopes and aims endlessly serve to provide too much stress

indicators.note: capricious means whimsical and changeable, so the letters are rearranged at whim

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of aims is dropped

parts.note: loses its final S
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fickle dreams and ambitions only add to someone's stress.
explanation.walkthrough: HOPES, AIM (aims without its end) and SERVE are rearranged; 'and' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To overemphasise is to give something more weight or importance than it merits, putting excessive stress on it.

clue.text: Low-cost launching with no public backing initially a pig to sort out

indicators.note: to sort out is to put in order, so these letters are rearranged
takes the first letter of each of the words no, public and backing

parts.note: first letter N
first letter P
first letter B
taken as written

explanation.surface: A startup launched without public funding proves a nightmare to put right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no public backing' looks like part of the definition, but its first letters N, P, B join A PIG TO SORT to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootstrapping is starting a business on minimal resources, self-funded rather than raising outside capital.

clue.text: I may hold up trains going by the Tube

parts.note: via means by way of
a duct is a tube or channel

explanation.surface: A London Underground worker admits to delaying services while travelling on the Tube.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is not the London Underground here, just a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A viaduct is a long bridge carrying a railway across a valley, literally supporting the trains above.

clue.text: Laid-back politician to lead a new party? It's out of the question

indicators.note: the politician comes at the front of what follows
laid back as in lying backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: Con is short for a Conservative politician
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A relaxed politician proposes heading a fresh party, but the idea is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid-back' sounds like relaxed, but it turns CON round.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is an informal phrase of refusal, saying something is impossible.

clue.text: Bounders needing time to settle

parts.note: kangaroos, roos for short, bound along

explanation.surface: Cads need a while before they calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounders' wants to mean cads; it is kangaroos that bound.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds roost when they come to rest for the night on a perch, settling down.

clue.text: Make a meal of covering over most of route to Stone

indicators.note: turned over, so the covering word reads backwards

parts.note: a top is a covering or lid

indicators.note: all but the last letter of road

parts.note: a road is a route
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the imperial weight

explanation.surface: Someone resurfaces nearly all of the road to Stone, a Staffordshire town, and makes a big fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a meal of' usually means to overdo something; here it literally means cook. A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To pot-roast is to cook meat slowly in a covered pot, which is literally preparing a dish.

clue.text: Former striker appearing before union rep?

indicators.note: the striker comes in front of the former

parts.note: a match is struck to light it
a maker is one who forms something

explanation.surface: An ex-footballer turns up ahead of a trade union official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former striker' reads as a retired footballer, but it is two pieces; the union is a marriage, not a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchmaker arranges marriages, acting on behalf of a couple's union, so is jokingly its representative.

clue.text: Dressing informally — a month with nothing on

definitions.text: Dressing informally — a month with nothing on

parts.words: Dressing informally — a month with nothing on
parts.note: the casual short name for this dressing is spelt by a month followed by a ring-shaped zero for nothing

explanation.walkthrough: The informal short form MAYO is MAY plus O (nothing) placed on it; the full dressing is the answer. The surface suggests going naked in May.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayonnaise is a salad dressing made from egg yolks and oil, colloquially shortened to mayo.

clue.text: Camp constituent's almost the centre of attention

indicators.note: the core of the word with nearly everything kept but its ends

explanation.surface: Something camp nearly becomes the focus of everyone's eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' looks like the flamboyant adjective but it is a campsite; the inner run of attention gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A campsite is made up of shelters, so one canvas shelter is a component of a camp.

clue.text: Novel drone perhaps given directions to unlicensed premises

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard
a drone is a male bee
N and S, north and south, are compass directions

explanation.surface: A fictional drone is sent off to illegal drinking dens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective for the drone, but it is the book She.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an Irish or Scottish term for an illicit bar selling alcohol without a licence.

clue.text: Dislike putting cap on expenditure at the outset

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat

indicators.note: only the start of expenditure is wanted

parts.note: first letter E

explanation.surface: Someone objects to limiting spending from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting cap on' reads as a spending limit, but the cap is a hat placed before E.
explanation.definitionFit: To hate is to feel intense aversion, a stronger form of dislike.

clue.text: Instruments not fit to hold a note when set up

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means raised, so the letters read from the bottom upwards
the unfit word holds the note inside it

parts.note: inapt means unsuitable
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Musical instruments not fit to sustain a note once they have been assembled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' suggests assembling the drums, but in a down clue it means the whole thing reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are kettledrums, the tuned percussion instruments of an orchestra.

clue.text: Version of Pooh in dodgy Arabic's something dreadful

indicators.note: puts one jumbled name inside the other
dodgy means unreliable, so the letters of Arabic are rearranged
a version of the name is a reworking of its letters

explanation.surface: A dubious Arabic translation of Winnie-the-Pooh turns out to be terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: Arabic rearranged gives ACR and BIA either side of OPHO, a jumble of Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrophobia is a fear of heights, so it is literally something full of dread.

clue.text: Went over the top visiting Bradford on vacation

indicators.note: the top goes into the emptied Bradford
vacated, so emptied of all but its outer letters

parts.note: outer letters B and D
a ridge is the top of a hill or roof

explanation.surface: Someone overreached on a holiday visit to Bradford, a city in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went over the top' wants to be the idiom for overdoing it; the top is the ridge inside BD.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridge a gap or river is to span it, crossing over from one side to the other.

clue.text: Once legendary figure losing head in battle

indicators.note: puts the beheaded figure inside the battle

parts.note: the Somme was a First World War battle

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

parts.note: the yeti is a legendary creature of the Himalayas

explanation.surface: A former hero of legend was beheaded in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sometime, as an adjective, means former, as in a sometime professor, the same as once.

clue.text: Tense, and ready to show guts

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
ripe means ready, as of fruit

explanation.surface: Someone nervous yet prepared to show courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guts' suggests bravery but means innards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is the stomach lining of cattle eaten as food, so it is literally animal guts.

clue.text: Setback involving minute vehicle used in Sky promotion?

indicators.note: wraps around the minute letter

parts.note: a blip is a minor temporary setback

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's marketing hits a snag over a tiny car.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky looks like the TV company, but it is the literal sky, where airships carry adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: A blimp is a non-rigid airship, often flown overhead carrying advertising.

clue.text: Some quasi-autonomous region

indicators.note: only some of the letters, a run inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Part of a semi-independent territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the world's largest continent, a vast part of the globe.

clue.text: Cook, exhausted after mains, is beginning to be ill

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of is counts

parts.note: first letter I

indicators.note: emptied out, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: outer letters C and K

explanation.surface: A chef, worn out after serving the main courses, starts to feel unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mains' suggests main courses, but it is the seas.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasick describes nausea caused by a ship's motion, a specific way of being unwell.

clue.text: England overwhelmed by crazy revolutionary arm

indicators.note: England is engulfed by the reversed word
revolving, so the crazy word is turned round

parts.note: nuts means crazy

explanation.surface: England swamped by a mad rebel with a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten gun was a British submachine gun of the Second World War, and arm means a weapon.

clue.text: Something at the drugstore excited almost 90% of American coeds

indicators.note: stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: seven of its eight letters, 87.5 per cent, is close to ninety, so the final letter is cut
taken as written

explanation.surface: Female students in the US get worked up at the pharmacy.
explanation.walkthrough: AMERICA (87.5% of American) and COEDS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A US drugstore traditionally had a soda fountain serving sweet fizzy drinks topped with a scoop of ice cream.
